what:
aide-memory is FREE but CLOSED-SOURCE. Source lives in the private `ahmedmmeky/aide-v0` repo; the public repo `aide-memory/aide-memory` contains only README, LICENSE, release workflow, issue templates, and post-binary release artifacts. Binary distribution partly protects the source. Model is free-as-in-beer, NOT free-as-in-speech — similar to Discord/Zoom.

PROHIBITED framings in any public-facing copy: "open source", "fully open", "source available", "free and open", "forkable", plus any `git clone + npm install + npm test` block that implies the public repo contains buildable source. ACCEPTABLE replacements: "free", "free to install", "free, private to your team", "free, memories live in your git repo", "no cloud dependency", "your data never leaves your repo", "private-by-default" (about memories, not source). Contribution sections should be recast as "Issues & feedback" pointing at the GitHub issues endpoint — no clone/install instructions for the public repo.
why: Critical correction from Apr 20, 2026 rebrand session. The first draft of the external-content rebrand led with "Free and open" framing; the user corrected that aide-memory is closed-source and flagged all open-source adjacent framings as prohibited. Any future external copy work (docs, marketing, landing, launch posts, public README) must apply this rule. Priority: always, because a slipup here misrepresents the product's licensing/IP posture, not just marketing tone.
